newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK to lobby France, Germany on future travel access.
newsitem.headline: HK to lobby France, Germany on future travel access.

text.p: Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten pledged on Sunday to press for easy access to France and Germany for holders of the territory's passports issued after it reverts to China next year.
The two are prominent among European ports of call in a campaign to lobby countries for easy access to Hong Kong travvellers under Beijing's rule from next July.
"I will be pressing them (France and Germany) to ensure that there is the easiest possible access for people with passports from Hong Kong to travel after 1997," Patten told reporters.
The British colony reverts to Chinese rule on July 1 and becomes a Special Administrative Region (SAR) of China.

After the handover, the new Hong Kong authority will issue SAR passports to eligible citizens. But very few major countries apart from Britain have said so far they will recognise the SAR passport and allow visa-free access.

"I think that the main issue there, as far as France and Germany are concerned, is to try to ensure that the question of entry by SAR passport holders to member states of the European Union is a matter for national decision and that the SAR passport is not placed on what is called the Common Visa List which would mean that there was then no distinction between the SAR passport and the PRC (People's Republic of China) passport," Patten said.

"The European Union, which has such a large stake in Hong Kong, must understand the importance to Hong Kong of the easiest possible travel and of the easiest possible access for our people with our passports to their countries," he said.

Patten departs on Sunday evening for Britain, and will then visit France and Germany before flying back to the territory on Friday, the day when Lu Ping, director of China's Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office, will visit Hong Kong.
Patten said time might not allow them to meet.

"But if Director Lu wishes to see me or to see the Chief Secretary Anson Chan then we would be happy to see him if it was possible. But I repeat, my diary, unless we could meet in mid-air, seems to make it rather difficult," he said.
"I can't change my return now, but if he would like to stay on for a few hours I would be delighted to see him," he added.

Patten said he would also be pleased to meet Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen in the future even though such a meeting might not be possible on Friday when Qian is scheduled to visit the territory.

"I understand Mr Qian will be coming on future occasions as well and anytime Mr Qian Qichen would like to see the Governor or the Chief Secretary of Hong Kong we would be delighted to see him," he said.
